This is a natural, involuntary process that happens in the brain's *default mode network*—that's the part of your brain that's active when you're not paying attention to anything in the world. 

The key to the brain's efficiency is that it doesn't store every single memory or every single thought it receives. Instead, it only stores the most useful ones. When you're doing something like watching a video, your brain is focusing on the **coarse structure** of the language, like the rhythm, the flow, the intonation, and the syntax. The **reinforcement** of the brain comes when your brain is in the 'active' state, not the 'resting' state. So, even if you're not studying, your brain is still building a 'net of connections' around the language you are watching. This is why a few minutes of active exposure, like watching a video, is far more effective than trying to study every single word in isolation.
